title: Playwright Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Playwright lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: A browser test
entries.summary: A browser test opens a page and checks what a person can do. setContent gives this test a tiny page without a website server.
notes: Install Playwright and its browser with the official setup guide before running a test file.

entries.name: Find by role
entries.summary: A role describes what an element does. A button role and its name make a locator that resembles how a person finds the control.
notes: A button with no useful name is hard for both people and tests to find.

entries.name: Labels identify inputs
entries.summary: A label tells a person what an input is for. getByLabel uses that relationship.
notes: Placeholder text is not a substitute for a persistent label.

entries.name: Click an action
entries.summary: click asks Playwright to perform a real user-like click. Check the visible result, not only that the click method returned.
notes: A successful click alone does not prove the intended action happened.

entries.name: Assertions wait for a result
entries.summary: Playwright locator assertions retry for a short time. This helps when a visible change happens after the action.
notes: Avoid fixed sleeps when you can wait for a real condition.

entries.name: Count repeated items
entries.summary: A locator can match several elements. toHaveCount checks how many matches exist.
notes: A count alone does not check the text of every item.

entries.name: Check a checkbox
entries.summary: check sets a checkbox to checked. It is clearer than clicking when the desired state is known.
notes: Clicking a box twice can return it to the original state.

entries.name: Select an option
entries.summary: A select input stores an option value. The label shown to people can differ from that value.
notes: Use selectOption for a native select, not for every custom menu.

entries.name: Test keyboard access
entries.summary: A keyboard test checks focus and key actions. It can reveal a control that works only with a mouse.
notes: Visible focus should remain easy to see on the real page.

entries.name: Mock a page response
entries.summary: A route handler can provide a known response. The test controls the content without calling a real external service.
notes: Register the route before the request it must catch.

entries.name: Isolate test state
entries.summary: Each Playwright test normally gets a fresh browser context. A context separates saved state such as cookies between tests.
notes: Do not rely on test order to create the state a test needs.

entries.name: Capture useful evidence
entries.summary: A screenshot records visible state. It helps explain a failure but is not a replacement for a precise behaviour check.
notes: Do not approve changed visual snapshots without looking at the changes.
